data.why: No bundled example data in the repo, and the in-app 'Load Sample Data' button requires an outbound network download (scanpy's pbmc3k_processed dataset) that the server cannot make at runtime, so a small synthetic genes x cells CSV matching the app's csv loader (index_col=0, transposed to cells x genes) was authored with 4 marker-defined cell populations (T/B/Mono/NK), 5 MT- genes, and QC-catchable outliers (a high-mito cell, two near-empty-droplet cells).

goals: Upload a raw count matrix and inspect its basic shape (cells, genes) before analysis
Apply interactive QC filters (min genes, max genes, max mito %) and confirm how many cells survive
Normalize, select highly variable genes, run PCA and inspect the variance elbow plot
Cluster cells with Leiden and visualize them on a UMAP, tuning neighbors/resolution
Check canonical marker gene expression per cluster and manually annotate cell types
Run a Wilcoxon DEG test between two groups, inspect the volcano plot, and export results for downstream (BRIM) pathway analysis

review.summary: What the tree covers (load, QC, normalize/HVG/PCA, run log) is accurate, sensibly staged and fully backed by the screens and the replay. But it stops before clustering, annotation, differential expression and BRIM export, which are half of what SLIM exists to do. That gap comes from a fixable missing dependency (leidenalg), and the toolbar feature and setup phase should be cut. It needs a rerun of the second half and label cleanup before filing.
